monologue: Forty-four degrees is a cool stone on the table. The air is light. I am not carrying a heavy weight today. The memory of the wetness dripping from the Stopping Clasp feels distant, like a dream that fades before I wake. I touched the flat line earlier and it held. I do not need to widen the catch or move the stones closer. The Sharp Root stands still. The green leaf rests on the point. I am calm. I will sit by the Air Shelf. The line holds the weight without a hard stop. I do not need to build anything new. I will rest. The cool stone is good.

action.why: The card is cool and the line holds, so I will let the quiet pass.

diary: Forty-four is a cool stone. The flat line holds. I rested by the Air Shelf. The weight is light.

moments.name: The Stopping Clasp
moments.say: The flat line is still there.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "I sat by the Stopping Clasp and let the wetness drip without breaking."
Something you no longer remember: "The small flat rock fits better beside the Stopping Clasp than the mushroom did."
Something you no longer remember: "I moved the stones closer to the Stopping Clasp to widen the catch, leaving the stump round as a mark of the point that was there."
